_readme: P1 Grand Challenges (decided 2026-10-02; master handoff §14, capability ladder §4.1 and §26): small problems prove principles, big projects change capability. A challenge opens when the work has raised its question; each stage is a chunky project (months, Attention a month, gold in aurei at AD 155 prices) that moves a capability, never a run of micro-scenes. A stage may need a resource Rome doesn't hand a stranger: the 'source' requirements (people.json syntax) get it at the stated price, otherwise it costs 'withoutSource' times as much. Amounts PROPOSED P1-10.

challenges.name: Measurement and standards
challenges.question: Can another workshop make a part that fits without seeing the original?
challenges.openText: Cassianus's pump has a seat that wore out. The bronzesmith on the Clivus cut a new one by eye, and it leaks. Your seats were cut to your own foot and your own rule; his are cut to his. Until two shops measure the same way, every repair is a new pump.

stages.name: A master foot in hard bronze

resource.name: tin bronze for a master that won't wear
resource.note: Good tin comes through Ostia, and the guild's shippers sell it to men they've eaten with. A stranger pays twice.

stages.text: The founder pours the bar twice before it comes out without a flaw. You file the ends square and mark the foot and its sixteen fingers. It is heavier than anything it will ever measure.

stages.name: Two shops agree on the foot
stages.needsText: Another shop has to agree to work to your foot, and no shop will take a stranger's word for it. You need someone who knows the shops.
stages.text: Felix brings the bronzesmith from the Clivus and a fitter from Ostia to your bench. They check their rules against your bar, argue for an afternoon, and go home with copies. A month later their seats match yours.

stages.name: Fit and no-fit gauges in hard steel

resource.name: Noric steel that holds an edge
resource.note: The best steel comes over the Alps from Noricum, and the merchants who carry it sell to guild members first.

stages.text: Two plugs for every bore: one that must go in, one that must not. The smith hardens them in oil and swears at the one that cracks. The second pair holds.

stages.name: A part made in another shop fits
stages.text: The fitter at Ostia cuts a seat to the gauges and sends it up the river in a box. It drops into Cassianus's pump without a file touching it. The bronzesmith asks for a set of gauges of his own and pays for them.

challenges.completeText: Three shops now cut seats to one set of gauges, and a seat from one fits a pump from another. Nobody calls it a standard. They say the parts are cut to the foreigner's foot.
